brightness_by_class: Per-video mean brightness of aligned face crops (train + development videos; test excluded); class differences show cues a detector could exploit.
brightness_vs_sharpness: Each point is one video (train + development videos; test excluded); overlap between classes indicates that simple image statistics alone cannot separate attacks from bona fide presentations.
class_balance_by_split: Every split has equal bona fide, print and replay counts; attacks outnumber bona fide videos 1980:990, so APCER and BPCER must be reported separately rather than as a single accuracy.
contrast_by_class: Per-video mean contrast of aligned face crops (train + development videos; test excluded).
dev_score_hist: Distribution of development video scores; attacks to the right of the dashed threshold are accepted as bona fide (APCER errors).
dev_threshold_curve: The operating threshold is the development-set point where APCER and BPCER are closest (ties: lower ACER, then higher threshold) and is frozen before any test evaluation.
duration_distribution: Distribution of video durations reported by ffprobe for each class.
frame_count_distribution: Distribution of decoded frame counts per video for every Protocol II video.
missing_failed_items: Counts of items that failed each data-quality check; zero bars confirm the check passed for every Protocol II video.
phone_distribution: Every phone contributes the same number of videos per class, so no single phone dominates the data.
session_distribution: Every session contributes the same number of videos per class, so no single session dominates the data.
sharpness_by_class: Per-video mean sharpness of aligned face crops (train + development videos; test excluded); recapture through print or screen often changes high-frequency detail.
subjects_per_split: No subject appears in more than one split, so test performance measures generalization to unseen people.
test_roc: ROC curves separate print and replay attacks from bona fide presentations; curves closer to the top-left corner indicate better separation.
test_score_hist: Distribution of test video scores; attacks to the right of the dashed threshold are accepted as bona fide (APCER errors).
training_curves: The checkpoint with the lowest development loss is selected; the test split is never used during training or model selection.
